summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia s/p allogeneic cord blood transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease, was admitted for worsening joint pain, fatigue, and nausea. His pain had increased after reducing OxyContin and stopping Plaquenil due to nausea. Labs showed elevated CRP indicating inflammation, but no infection. Prednisone was increased to 20mg daily, OxyContin was resumed twice daily, and morphine was provided for breakthrough pain due to oxycodone shortage. He developed transient hypotension attributed to narcotics, which resolved with dose adjustment. Podiatry removed bilateral ingrown toenails; a minor infection was treated with Keflex and topical antibiotic. Constipation and GERD were managed with senna/Colace and twice-daily esomeprazole. His pain, fatigue, and nausea improved, and he was discharged home in good condition with updated medications and follow-up plans.
problems: Pain in joint, other specified sites
Acute myeloid leukemia, without mention of having achieved remission
